title: Micro-Mobility Services
desc: Plan and run a small shared bike or scooter service: fleet, safety, parking, pricing, maintenance and city rules.
outcomes: Explain micro-mobility types and where they fit.
Plan fleet size, zones and parking.
task: Plan a 30-day pilot of a shared micro-mobility service for one campus or district, with fleet, safety rules, maintenance, pricing and a community plan.
condition: A computer, a map, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. Real vehicles are not required.
standard: Fleet and cost maths correct; safety rules and rider age limits stated; parking and permits checked; maintenance plan has daily checks; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Campus managers, tourism staff, city assistants, entrepreneurs.
evidence: zone map, fleet sheet, safety rules, price sheet, maintenance plan
modules: Bikes, e-bikes, scooters and cargo bikes have different range, speed and cost.
Short trips under 5 km are the main use.
E-assist helps on hills and with longer trips.
Match to local roads, weather and rules.
A hilly campus picks e-bikes because they allow fast trips up slopes without sweat.
Compare three vehicle types in a table.
Table includes range, cost and best use.
Order on the street keeps the service welcome.
Marked parking, no-go zones and speed limits.
Work with the owner or authority.
Parking bays at gates reduce clutter; a no-go zone near a hospital entrance prevents blocked access.
Draw a zone map for a campus or district.
Not too many and not too few.
Fleet = peak trips / trips per vehicle per day.
Rebalancing moves vehicles from places where they pile up to where they are needed.
60 peak trips at 6 trips per vehicle need 10 vehicles plus 2 spares.
Size a fleet for your case.
Helmets, lights, speed limits and age limits.
Rider tips and clear rules in the app.
A slow-speed zone is set near pedestrians and the speed is limited remotely.
Daily check: brakes, tyres, lights, bell and lock.
A tag shows last check date; vehicles failing a check are removed.
Unlock fee plus per-minute price; passes.
Costs: vehicles, staff, charging, repair, insurance and permits.
Discounts for students and low-income riders.
Break-even is 4.2 trips per vehicle per day at a 20 INR average fare.
A fine for blocking paths is explained in rules and enforced fairly.
Targets for trips, safety and complaints.
Decide to stop, change or grow.
The pilot adds two bays after complaints and raises utilisation.
quiz: Typical trip length?
Under about 5 km. (Covered in module 1: Types and fit. To pass that module: Table includes range and cost.)
Fleet formula?
Peak trips / trips per vehicle per day. (Covered in module 2: Zones and parking. To pass that module: Zones marked.)
Name a safety rule.
Helmets or speed limits. (Covered in module 3: Fleet sizing. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Daily check items?
Brakes, tyres, lights, bell, lock. (Covered in module 4: Safety. To pass that module: Rules measurable.)
Break-even idea?
Trips per day needed to cover costs. (Covered in module 5: Maintenance and charging. To pass that module: Card has ten items.)
Why parking zones?
To avoid clutter. (Covered in module 6: Pricing and money. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
Why insurance?
Covers incidents. (Covered in module 7: Community and environment. To pass that module: Each has an owner.)
What is rebalancing?
Moving vehicles to demand. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers can follow it.)
Name a community issue.
Noise or blocked paths. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers can follow it.)
What is a pilot?
A short test before scaling. (Covered in module 8: Pilot plan. To pass that module: Peers can follow it.)
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others

ladder: Types and fit

L1: learner can name types. Focus module: Types and fit (Understand, 3 h). Bikes, e-bikes, scooters. Key points: Short trips under 5 km are the main use. E-assist helps hills. Match to local roads and weather.

Teach: open with the worked example. A hilly campus picks e-bikes. Then set the activity: Compare 3 types. Mark against the standard: Table includes range and cost. Check at this level: Typical trip length? Model answer: Under about 5 km. Types.
Zones and parking

L2: learner knows safety rules. Focus module: Zones and parking (Apply, 4 h). Order on the street. Key points: Pick start points near demand. Marked parking, no-go zones, speed limits. Work with the owner or authority.

Teach: open with the worked example. Parking bays at gates reduce clutter. Then set the activity: Draw a zone map. Mark against the standard: Zones marked. Check at this level: Fleet formula? Model answer: Peak trips / trips per vehicle per day. Rules.
Fleet sizing

L3: learner can plan zones. Focus module: Fleet sizing (Analyse, 4 h). Not too many, not too few. Key points: Fleet = peak trips / trips per vehicle per day. Rebalancing moves bikes to demand. Start small and measure.

Teach: open with the worked example. 60 peak trips at 6 trips each need 10 bikes plus a spare. Then set the activity: Size your fleet. Mark against the standard: Maths correct. Check at this level: Name a safety rule. Model answer: Helmets or speed limits. Map.
Safety

L4: learner can run daily checks. Focus module: Safety (Evaluate, 5 h). Prevent injury. Key points: Helmets, lights, speed limits; age limits. Rider training and clear rules. Incident log and insurance.

Teach: open with the worked example. A slow-speed zone is set near pedestrians. Then set the activity: Write safety rules. Mark against the standard: Rules measurable. Check at this level: Daily check items? Model answer: Brakes, tyres, lights, bell, lock. Checks.
Maintenance and charging

L5: learner can price and size. Focus module: Maintenance and charging (Apply, 4 h). Safe vehicles every day. Key points: Daily check: brakes, tyres, lights, bell, lock. Battery swaps and safe charging. Spare parts.

Teach: open with the worked example. A tag shows last check date. Then set the activity: Create a check card. Mark against the standard: Card has ten items. Check at this level: Break-even idea? Model answer: Trips per day needed to cover costs. Sums.
Community and environment

L6: learner can lead operations. Focus module: Community and environment (Evaluate, 3 h). Be a good neighbour. Key points: Noise, sidewalk clutter, accessibility. Complaint line. Recycling of batteries and parts.

Teach: open with the worked example. A fine for blocking paths is explained in rules. Then set the activity: List community actions. Mark against the standard: Each has an owner. Check at this level: Why parking zones? Model answer: To avoid clutter. Team.
Pilot plan
L7: learner can audit a pilot. Focus module: Pilot plan (Create, 4 h). Run 30 days. Key points: Targets for trips, safety and complaints. Review weekly. Decide to stop, change or grow.

Teach: open with the worked example. The pilot adds two bays after complaints. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Peers can follow it. Check at this level: Why insurance? Model answer: Covers incidents. Peer audit.
